paidMemberships.stalenessNote: STALE BY DESIGN, DISCLOSED: 277.65M is Netflix's LAST FILED global streaming paid membership count, as of June 30, 2024. Netflix discontinued quarterly membership reporting after Q4 2024; no later membership figure appears in any subsequent 10-Q or 10-K, including the Q2 2026 10-Q (accession 0001065280-26-000212), which OP searched end to end. This is therefore the most recent FILED figure available, not a current one, and it is used as the per-user median basis on that basis. As of the 2026-09-02 valuation date the figure is approximately 26 months old. Any user comparing it against a current subscriber estimate is comparing against a different measurement; this note exists so that gap is visible rather than implied.

citation.exhibit: Exhibit 99.1 - Q2 2024 shareholder letter, summary results table, row 'Global Streaming Paid Memberships'
citation.correction: P10.7 F1. The prior citation (0001065280-26-000212, the Q2 2026 Form 10-Q) does NOT contain 277,650 / 277.6 / any paid-membership or subscriber count; Netflix discontinued quarterly membership reporting, and the only 'members' occurrence in that filing is deferred-revenue prose. The VALUE ITSELF IS CORRECT AND UNCHANGED: the Q2 2024 shareholder letter (accession 0001065280-24-000199, Exhibit 99.1) reports 'Global Streaming Paid Memberships 238.39 247.15 260.28 269.60 277.65' for Q2'23 through Q2'24, so 277.65M is the Q2 2024 figure. The defect was the period label ('Q2 2026') and the accession, not the number. Root cause: a Q2 2024 figure was relabelled to the current quarter and pointed at a filing that never carried it. Corrected here by re-pointing to the originating document and restating the period as Q2 2024.

arm.period: Q2 2024 (three months ended 2024-06-30) - derived, not printed
arm.stalenessNote: STALE BY DESIGN, DISCLOSED: $11.64 is derived from Netflix's LAST period in which both ARM inputs were filed (Q2 2024, as of June 30, 2024) - the same vintage as the 277.65M memberships basis it accompanies. Netflix discontinued quarterly membership reporting after Q4 2024 and its 10-K filings carry no ARM disclosure at all, so no later ARM input exists to derive from. As of the 2026-09-02 valuation date the basis is approximately 26 months old. This record is a context display string only: src/engine/methods/perUser.js consumes arm.display as arpuContext.peerArpu and no per-share computation reads arm.value.
arm.derivation: ARM per the filer's own definition in the Q2 2024 shareholder letter ('ARM (Average Revenue per Membership) is defined as streaming revenue divided by the average number of streaming paid memberships'): Q2 2024 revenue $9,559M / average paid memberships (269.60 + 277.65) / 2 = 273.625M / 3 months = $11.6449 -> $11.64. Both inputs from the letter summary results table (Revenue 8187 / 8542 / 8833 / 9370 / 9559; Global Streaming Paid Memberships 238.39 / 247.15 / 260.28 / 269.60 / 277.65). Headline revenue used as the streaming-revenue input; the DVD segment wound down in 2023 so the residual definitional gap sits inside the stated tolerance.

citation.exhibit: Exhibit 99.1 - Q2 2024 shareholder letter: summary results table (revenue + memberships inputs) and ARM definition footnote; value derived, not printed
citation.correction: P10.7 F1 (Resubmission 4). The prior record carried value $12.10 with period 'Q2 2026' cited to the Q2 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 MD&A (accession 0001065280-26-000212), which states no ARM figure anywhere (OP-searched end to end). A live EDGAR sweep this turn further proves $12.10 appears in NO Netflix primary document: absent from the Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 2024 and Q1/Q2/Q3 2025 shareholder letters (which print only regional ARM, never a $12.10 global figure) and from the 2024 and 2025 10-K filings (which carry no ARM disclosure at all). The value was therefore REPLACED, not re-pointed: $11.64 derived per the filer's definition from the last period with both inputs filed. Root cause: an unverified $12.10 was stored against a current-quarter label and a filing that never carried it. Computational impact: zero - perUser.js:194 reads only the display string as arpuContext.peerArpu; paidMemberships.value and capitalizedEnterpriseValue (the median-driving inputs) are untouched, so the Per-User median 347.91 and all pins are unmoved.
